# s09 — Fail when a profile's required font is missing

WeasyPrint substitutes a fallback font without an error when a stylesheet
names a font that is not installed. A build with `font-family: "NoSuchFont"`
exits 0 and embeds Verdana.

**Findings:** G5 · **Size:** M · **Tree:** core

**Not in this slice:** checking fonts named only in `--css` stylesheets;
installing fonts; parsing font stacks out of CSS.

## Why

branded-pdf (xelatex) fails loudly when a brand font is missing. Quire
instead produces a document that looks almost right in the wrong typeface,
which is easy to send out unnoticed. A profile already knows which fonts it
depends on and can declare them.

## Files

- `quire.py` (`load_profile`, `_load_variant`, `plan_job`)
- `test_quire.py`
- `docs/profiles.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

## Failing tests

- `fonts = ["A", "B"]` at profile level is parsed; a variant-level `fonts`
  list replaces it for that variant; a non-list or non-string entry is an error.
- With a stubbed font lookup, a missing declared font fails planning with an
  error naming the font and the profile, before anything is written.
- When every declared font is present, planning succeeds.
- When the lookup tool is unavailable, planning warns once on stderr and
  continues.
- A profile without `fonts` behaves as before.

## Implement

Add an optional `fonts` list to `profile.toml` (profile level and per variant).
At plan time, check each family with `fc-list` (`fc-list : family`), which ships
with fontconfig, a WeasyPrint dependency; match family names case-insensitively
against the comma-separated family names fontconfig reports. Keep the lookup in
one function so tests can stub it. Fail with
`error: profile <name> needs font "<family>", which is not installed`.
Document the key and note that fonts embedded through `@font-face` need not be
listed.

## Check

- `python3 test_quire.py`
- Real build with a scratch profile that lists one installed and one
  nonexistent font; report the error text.
